answer: When the spring flood comes the census keeper counts every palm in the oasis and writes the number in the census book, and the harvest shares follow that count. A forge palm counted twice fails the census: at the nebula of the grove the trunks must stand where the book lists them, and a double-counted palm steals another family's dates. Faking the census means bribing the keeper, forging 12 years of counts and paying 9,600, while the vault figure in the census book is read at every harvest, so a palm that was never counted bears no share.
